pill.desc: lyophilized powder in a single-dose vial

clues.kinetics: Subcutaneous bioavailability is about 89% of intravenous, and urine is the primary route of elimination, carrying 85% of an intravenous dose.
clues.substance: The active moiety has a molecular weight of 244.2, and it is sparingly soluble in water but soluble in dimethylsulfoxide.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as 100 mg single-dose vials, given daily for 7 days in a 28-day cycle.
clues.safety: No boxed warning. Contraindicated in advanced malignant hepatic tumors and in hypersensitivity to the drug or to mannitol; petechiae and rigors are common.
clues.indication: Myelodysplastic syndrome subtypes and chronic myelomonocytic leukemia in adults, and newly diagnosed juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia in children.
clues.mechanism: Causes hypomethylation of DNA and direct cytotoxicity to abnormal bone marrow cells. Dividing cells are the main target, since non-proliferating cells are relatively insensitive.

tell: A cytidine analog cleared mostly in urine, with subcutaneous dosing nearly as bioavailable as intravenous.
